species.name: Brewlet

dex.text: A china teapot that has become, against all odds, a person. It steams politely when it is happy and boils over when it is not.
dex.fact: The Potteries, six towns around Stoke-on-Trent, became the centre of English ceramics, home to names such as Wedgwood, Spode and Minton.

species.real: Bone china, made with ash from animal bones, was perfected in Staffordshire in the late 1700s and is surprisingly tough for something so delicate.

species.name: Brownbetty

dex.text: A great round pot in a knitted cosy, and the only golem in the Isles who will ask whether you take milk. Do not say no.
dex.fact: The Brown Betty is a round brown teapot long made in Staffordshire from local red clay, and plenty of tea drinkers swear by it.

species.real: Britain drinks about a hundred million cups of tea a day, and a fair few of them go cold while someone is talking.
